title: Save a small local picture
summary: imwrite saves image pixels to a file. Check its return value and choose a practice path so you do not overwrite work you need.
introduction: imwrite saves image pixels to a file. Check its return value and choose a practice path so you do not overwrite work you need. We will use a small example so you can follow each step.
learningObjectives: Explain save a small local picture
Use the example to answer a practice question

blocks.text: imwrite saves image pixels to a file. Check its return value and choose a practice path so you do not overwrite work you need.

blocks.code:
import cv2
import numpy as np

image = np.full((10, 10, 3), [0, 255, 0], dtype=np.uint8)
saved = cv2.imwrite("practice-green.png", image)
print(saved)
blocks.title: Save a small local picture

blocks.text: On a writable practice folder with PNG support, the output is True and a small green PNG file is saved. False or an error means the save did not succeed.

items: Read the example from top to bottom. Point to the part that uses the new idea.
Open the saved file locally and check its colour and size.
Explain what changed in your own words. Check the example again if you get stuck.

blocks.title: A common mistake
blocks.text: A saved picture is not uploaded anywhere by this code; sharing is a separate action.
For more detail later, use this [OpenCV further reading](https://docs.opencv.org/4.x/d6/d00/tutorial_py_root.html).
